key_insight: Specializing model components in a hierarchical pipeline (device/environment adapters → respiratory feature extractor → clinical QA head) makes question-answering from heterogeneous respiratory audio robust and clinically meaningful across real-world recording conditions.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between noisy, device- and environment-varying mobile respiratory audio and reliable clinical question-answering by isolating adaptation, representation, and reasoning stages so the system generalizes across acquisition heterogeneity.
method: Hierarchical architecture with specialized stages: low-level audio adapters for device/environment normalization, mid-level respiratory-sound feature extractor, and a high-level QA module for clinical reasoning.

Routing / mixture-of-experts style specialization and joint training pipeline (self-/contrastive pretraining on large respiratory audio pools + supervised QA fine-tuning) to improve robustness and transfer.
Clinical alignment mechanisms (constrained decoding, uncertainty calibration or rationale outputs) to ensure answers are clinically relevant and appropriately cautious.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building robust multimodal clinical assistants that handle variable real-world audio, improving generalization and trustworthiness of respiratory AI tools for screening and longitudinal monitoring.
visual_elements: Layered model diagram showing: raw audio → device/environment adapters → respiratory feature extractor → QA head (with arrows showing information flow).
Pipeline flowchart: recording (phones/environments) → preprocessing/adaptation → representation → question + answer, annotated with failure points and mitigations.
Bar/line chart comparing model performance/consistency across device types and noise levels (showing improved robustness).
Icon set: microphone/device diversity, waveform + filter icon (audio processing), stethoscope/medical note (clinical QA), shield (robustness/uncertainty).
paper_title: RAMoEA-QA: Hierarchical Specialization for Robust Respiratory Audio Question Answering
paper_authors: Gaia A. Bertolino, Yuwei Zhang, Tong Xia, Domenico Talia, Cecilia Mascolo
